div.head: I Cn 22
div.ab: And we lærað, þæt ælc Cristen man geleornige, þæt he huru cunne rihtne geleafan (⁊) ariht understandan ⁊ Pater noster ⁊ Credan geleornian.
We lærað, þæt ælc Cristen man geleornige, þæt he cunne huru rihtne geleafan ⁊ ariht understandan ⁊ Pater noster ⁊ Credan geleornian.
And we lærað, þæt alc Crysten man geleornige, þæt he huru cunne rihtne geleafan ariht understanden ⁊ Pater noster ⁊ Credo geleornian.
Et omnis Christianus addiscat, ut saltem sane fidei rectam intelligentiam habeat et sciat ‘Pater noster’ et ‘Credo in Deum’,
[22] Debet etiam quisque Christianus discere ‘Pater noster’ et ‘Credo in Deum’,
Hortamur quoque, ut omnis Christianus discat, quatinus nouerit saltem ueram fidem semper intelligere recte et Dominicam oracionem et catholicam fidem discat,
We lærað þæt ælc Cristen man geleornige þæt he cunne huru rihtne geleafan ariht understandan ⁊ Pater noster ⁊ Credan geleornian.
And we lærað, þæt ælc Cristen man geleornige, þæt he huru cunne rihtne geleafan and ariht understandan and Pater noster and Credan geleornian.
Und wir schreiben vor, dass jeder Christenmensch [so viel] lerne, dass er wenigstens das richtige Glaubensbekenntniss ordentlich verstehen und Pater noster und Credo lernen könne.
And we instruct that every Christian man learn [so much] that he can at least rightly understand the true faith, and learn the Pater noster and the Creed.
We enjoin that every Christian man apply himself until he can at least understand aright the true belief, and learn the Pater Noster and the Creed.
We instruct every Christian to study so that he can, in particular, know and properly understand the true faith and learn the Paternoster and Creed.
div.note: Vgl. Can. Eg. 22 | Vgl. Wulfstan p. 20

G's ‘⁊’ (compare B; ‘á’ compare Cons. ‘semper’) should be struck with A, Ld and Wulfstan (Liebermann). Liebermann compares the Canons of Edgar 22; Wulfstan p. 20.; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 303, October 2026 (MS Cons)
geleafan and ariht: geleafan ariht A

note.seg: ⁊ [vgl. B] á [vgl. semper Consil.] riht G; streiche ⁊ mit A Ld Wulfstan 20, Homilie nach Wulfstan 307.
⁊ [cf. B] á [cf. semper Consil.] riht G; delete ⁊ with A Ld Wulfstan 20, homily after Wulfstan 307.

Erste Zeilen + 22, 5 ähneln zumeist Can. Eadg., ed. Thorpe Anc. laws 397. Vielleicht nur durch Benutzung dieser selben Quelle klingt gleich der Homilet n. Wulfstan p. 39, den der andere p. 301f. wiederholt; der p. 33 hat nur Stücke davon. Aus 22 schöpft der p. 307. In sehr mit 22. 22, 1 ähnlichen Worten fordern, Glaubensbekenntnis (s. d. Gl 2) und Vaterunser zu kennen Ælfric Homil. ed. Thorpe I 274 = II 604; Homil. in Bibl. Agsä. Prosa ed. Assmann III 142. Gevatter soll dem Paten beides beibringen; Homil. c. 1000 ed. Brotanek Texte Altengl. Lit. 25. 109. 127.—Über Eadgars Fränk. Quelle Theodulf, die bei Thorpe Anc. laws 476 als Ecclesiast. institutes übersetzt steht, vgl. Hauck Kirchengesch. II 240¹; Böhmer Ki. u. Staat 51. 76

The first lines + 22, 5 mostly resemble Can. Eadg., ed. Thorpe Anc. laws 397. It is perhaps only through use of this same source that the Homilet n. Wulfstan p. 39, whom the other one repeats at p. 301f., sounds the same; the one at p. 33 has only parts of it. The one at p. 307 draws on 22. In words very similar to 22. 22, 1, knowledge of the Creed (see that word in Gl 2) and of the Lord’s Prayer is demanded by Ælfric Homil. ed. Thorpe I 274 = II 604; Homil. in Bibl. Agsä. Prosa ed. Assmann III 142. The godparent is to teach both to the godchild; Homil. c. 1000 ed. Brotanek Texte Altengl. Lit. 25. 109. 127.—On Eadgar’s Frankish source Theodulf, which appears in translation in Thorpe Anc. laws 476 as Ecclesiast. institutes, cf. Hauck Kirchengesch. II 240¹; Böhmer Ki. u. Staat 51. 76
Den schlechten Stil ‘lerne, dass er lerne’ verschuldet wohl die Benutzung der 2 Quellen: we lærað þæt ælc leornige þæt he cunne (Eadgar) und ælc cunne understandan Wulfstan
The poor style ‘learn, that he learn’ is probably due to the use of the 2 sources: we lærað þæt ælc leornige þæt he cunne (Eadgar) and ælc cunne understandan Wulfstan
geleafan rihtlice Wulfstan 20; also G's ⁊ á (semper) unauthentisch
geleafan rihtlice Wulfstan 20; G’s ⁊ á (semper) is therefore not authentic
Cf. Can. Edg. 22, ed. Thorpe, Anc. Laws, ii. p. 248; Can. Ælfric, 23, ibid. p. 351; Ælfric, Homilies, ed. Thorpe, i. p. 274; ii. p. 604; Wulfstan, pp. 33, 39, 301 f., 307.

geleornige…geleornian. This verb appears to be used in somewhat different senses here—intrans. in the former case, trans. in the latter. The passive idea (‘receive instruction’) is not actually contained in the first case, but in practice instruction would probably be involved.
